$comment: What the package-schema acceptance criterion answers on this tree, per assertion (D-110).
A two-way ratchet: the CI job fails when a run disagrees with this file in either direction.
Two of the nine are `fail` today and are supposed to be — a package still cannot be installed
end to end until feature 080's Wave 3 finishes. Recording that is what makes an accidental *green* as
visible as an accidental red: a change that quietly satisfied A4 without going through the
composition would show up here as drift, not as a pass nobody looked at.
Move an entry only in the merge request that earned the move, and never to make a pipeline
pass. When Wave 3 lands, every entry becomes `pass` and this file becomes the guard against
regressions rather than the record of a gap.
T031 moved A5 to `pass` (an installed package now reaches `resolvedManifestEntries()` and
both composition roots) and corrected A6's and A7's reasons, which had both read `Follows
A5` and stopped being true the moment A5 did.
T033 moved A1, A2, A3 and A4 to `pass` — the whole schema half. A package's migrations and
entities now reach the ORM through the async seam in `src/db/configured-migrations.ts` and
`src/db/configured-entities.ts`. Seven of the nine now pass. A6 and A7 stay `fail`, and A7's
reason moved: its migration count is settled and its blocker is now A6's, which is why
T033 did not close it.
T032 moved no status and rewrote A5's reason: the assertion now measures the bundles through
`reconcileBundles` and `translation_bundles` rather than reading the files itself, which is
what its own recorded reason named as still missing. A reason that has stopped being true is
drift this file cannot detect — only the status is compared — so it is corrected by hand in
the merge request that made it false, exactly as T031 did for A6 and A7.
T033a/T036 moved no status and rewrote A7's reason, which its own change falsified. A7 said
the missing `module_registrations` row 'is written by `loadModulePresence` during
`composeApp()`' and would follow from fixing A6's ordering. It will not: D-157.6(b) narrows
that reconciler's insert population to core plus overlay, so no boot will ever converge a
package. That is the ruled-correct behaviour — a boot that marks a package installed before
its migrations run is what made `module:install` a silent no-op — and it means A7's row now
has exactly one author, `install`, which since T036 the CLI can finally name.

A1.reason: Earned by T033 (P3 option A). The committed migration registry is still a walk of `backend/src` and still contributes no package entry — that is D-119's answer and it does not move. What moved is that the *configured* order is no longer the committed registry: `src/db/configured-migrations.ts` became an async factory that merges it with every installed package's `./migrations` export, tagged `origin: 'external'` so a stranger's stamp cannot join the frozen historical prefix. The probe reports the package's class applied alongside 158 core migrations.

A2.reason: Follows A1, and is kept separate from it on purpose: the table exists because the migration body ran.

A3.reason: The tenant column and the named index are both in `information_schema` as the package's migration declared them — `organization_id uuid` nullable, `acceptance_probe_rows_organization_id_index`. This is the assertion that distinguishes a migration that ran from a row in `mikro_orm_migrations` standing in for one.

A4.reason: Earned by T033. The source-text probe still cannot see a compiled decorator and never will, so the committed entity registry is unchanged; `src/db/configured-entities.ts` merges it at runtime with the entity classes each package's `./backend` export declares. `em.find(AcceptanceProbeRow, {})` returns against the host's own metadata.

A5.reason: Earned by T031 (P1) and **completed by T032 (P2)**, which moved no status and changed what the pass means. `loadPackageModuleEntries` (`src/packages/`) enumerates the instance's `node_modules`, keeps every package carrying `endora.type === "module"` whose install does not link out of the tree it was found under, and both composition roots now call `composeModules([...MODULES, ...overlay, ...packages], …)`. `resolvedManifestEntries()` merges the same discovery, so the module has an identity, its permission is grantable and the palette action resolves in `en` and `pl`. `filePath` is the resolved `package.json`, because `dirname(filePath)` is how the i18n reconciler and the orchestrator find a module's assets and the compiled root export's directory holds no `i18n/`. T032 replaced the assertion's own `loadModuleBundles` read with the platform's path: it runs `reconcileBundles` over the whole resolved set and then reads the action keys back out of `getMergedBundleForLanguage`, which is what the Admin SPA and the command palette serve from. The previous wording recorded exactly this as still outstanding. A package whose bundles the reconciler cannot reach now fails A5 with its `i18n/` sitting in `node_modules`, which is the case the old read could not distinguish from a pass.

A6.reason: No longer `follows A5` — the module is in the resolved set since T031, and this is still red for two reasons of its own. (1) `composition.ts` reconciles settings from `collectRegisteredSettingsManifests(REGISTERED_MANIFESTS)`, the bare-core registry, which is stated in its own comment as a deliberate cut; so a package's (and an overlay's) `settings` manifest reaches no reconciler and the activation row is never created. (2) The probe's `gate-off` phase reads the row before it composes anything, and no earlier phase composes the application, so on a fresh database no reconciler has run at all. Fixing (1) alone moves nothing, which is why it is not fixed here. Belongs with T032/T033, where the merged registry gets an owner (D-155.3(c)).

A7.reason: The blocker is still the missing `module_registrations` row — `uninstall` short-circuits on `already-uninstalled` because none exists for `acceptance_probe` — but **who is supposed to write it has changed, and this reason is rewritten by the merge request that changed it** (T033a, D-157.6(b)). It used to say the row is written by `loadModulePresence` during `composeApp()` and would follow from fixing A6's ordering. It will not, and must not: that reconciler inserts `state='installed'` for every manifest with no row, so a boot after `pnpm add` marked a package installed *before* any migration of its had run and turned `module:install` into a no-op that applied nothing and exited 0. Its insert population is now core plus the deployment's overlay. So A7's row has exactly one author — `install`, which applies the migrations, reconciles the settings and runs the hook — and the probe reaches it through no phase today: `gate-off` returns early on A6's missing activation Setting, and no phase installs. T036 removed the other half of that gap, the CLI answering `unknown module` for a package id, so the command that must write this row can at least name the module. The migration count itself is settled (T033): `revertMigrationsFor` takes an injected `MigrationOwnership`, `composition.ts` supplies the merged one, and the empty case refuses rather than warning, so a package cannot hard-uninstall to a warning and leave its table behind.

A8.reason: Passes today, and must: it measures the harness, not the platform. The tarball install resolves entirely inside the throwaway instance. An A8 that could not pass before Wave 3 would be an assertion nobody could trust after it.

A9.reason: Passes today, and must, for the same reason: A8 refuses the same package consumed by link from inside this repository. If A9 ever fails, A8 has stopped being able to say no and every other assertion is worth less.
